cards.text: Friend, this is a hard chapter, so I'm going to tell it straight and walk through it with you. It starts with Dinah, the daughter Leah had borne to Jacob. She goes out to visit the daughters of the land.
Shechem, son of Hamor the Hivite and prince of the region, sees her. He takes her and lies with her by force, and I'm not going to soften that for you, friend.

cards.question: After what he did, Shechem wants nothing more to do with Dinah.
The text says Shechem loves Dinah and speaks to her tenderly. Then he goes to his father Hamor. What does he tell him?

answers.text: Get me this girl as a wife
Send her back to her father

cards.text: Word reaches Jacob that Shechem has defiled his daughter Dinah. His sons are out in the field with the livestock, so watch closely what Jacob does next, friend.

cards.question: Jacob hears the news about Dinah, but his sons are away in the field. What does Jacob do?

answers.text: Goes to the city gate himself
Packs up the camp to leave

cards.text: Meanwhile, Hamor comes to speak with Jacob, and Jacob's sons hear what happened and come back from the field. Pay attention to who's walking in, friend, because this is where the whole story turns.

cards.question: When Jacob's sons hear what Shechem did to their sister, they are filled with ___ and ___.
The text calls what Shechem did to Dinah an outrage in Israel, a thing that should not be done.

cards.text: Then Hamor makes his case to Jacob and his sons: "My son Shechem longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as his wife."

cards.question: Hamor doesn't stop at one wedding. What else does he offer Jacob's family?

answers.text: To intermarry and settle in the land
To leave the region in peace
To rule the city alongside him

cards.text: Then Shechem himself speaks to Dinah's father and brothers: "Grant me this favor, and I will give you whatever you ask."

cards.question: Shechem wants Dinah as his wife, so he tells her family, "Demand a high ___ and an expensive gift, and I will give you whatever you ask."

cards.text: Jacob's sons answer Shechem and Hamor. But the text tells us up front: because Shechem had defiled their sister, they answer deceitfully.

cards.question: The brothers say giving their sister to an uncircumcised man would be a disgrace. What condition do they set for Hamor's city?

answers.text: Hamor must give up the city

cards.question: If the condition is met, the brothers say they will dwell among Hamor's people and become one people.
And if Hamor's men won't agree to be circumcised, what do the brothers say they'll do?

cards.text: The brothers' offer seems good to Hamor and his son Shechem. And Shechem, the most respected of all his father's household, doesn't hesitate.

cards.question: The text gives a reason Shechem doesn't hesitate to meet the brothers' condition: he is ___ with Jacob's daughter.

cards.text: So Hamor and Shechem go to the gate of their city to talk to the men there. Keep in mind what we already know, friend: the brothers answered deceitfully, and these two have no idea.

cards.question: At the city gate, Hamor and Shechem describe Jacob's family to the men of the city: "These men are at ___ with us."

cards.text: Then comes the catch. Jacob's family will only agree to be one people with them if all their men are circumcised.

cards.question: To win the men of the city over, Hamor and Shechem bring up the newcomers' livestock and possessions.

cards.text: And it works. Every man who went out of the city gate listens to Hamor and Shechem, and every male of the city is circumcised.

cards.question: Three days later, while the men of the city are still in pain, two of Dinah's brothers take their swords. Who are they?

cards.text: Simeon and Levi go into the unsuspecting city with their swords. Friend, this is what that deceitful answer was hiding all along.

cards.question: Simeon and Levi spare Hamor and his son Shechem.
Simeon and Levi slaughter every male in the city. Before they go away, who do they take out of Shechem's house?

cards.text: Then Jacob's other sons come upon the slaughter and loot the city, taking the flocks, the herds, the donkeys and everything else in the city and in the field. Friend, it doesn't stop with two brothers and two swords.

cards.question: The text says Jacob's other sons loot the city because their sister had been defiled.
The brothers plunder everything in the houses. They carry off all the possessions, along with the city's ___ and ___.

cards.text: Then Jacob speaks to Simeon and Levi: "You have brought trouble upon me by making me a stench to the Canaanites and Perizzites, the people of this land."

cards.question: Jacob tells Simeon and Levi his family is few in number. What does he say the people of the land might do?

answers.text: Drive his flocks out of Canaan
Refuse to trade with his family

cards.question: How do Simeon and Levi answer their father Jacob?

answers.text: They ask if Shechem should have treated Dinah that way
They say they are sorry for the trouble
They promise to make peace with the land

cards.text: And the chapter ends right there, on a question hanging in the air. Stay with me, friend. Jacob's story isn't done yet.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 13 quotes "Demand a high ___ and an expensive gift, and I will give you whatever you ask.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 4 quotes "These men are at ___ with us.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The BSB reads "Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the region," which leaves open whether the prince is Shechem or Hamor. The card says "son of Hamor the Hivite and prince of the region," which settles it as Shechem. Keeping the BSB's apposition, like "Shechem, son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the region," leaves it open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "finished" doesn't match the tone of the other answers and reads oddly. Right after the assault in this passage, "finished with Jacob's daughter" could also come across as crude. It needs a wrong answer that is a believable feeling, in the same tone as "delighted."

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The true-or-false statement only says Hamor and Shechem "bring up" the newcomers' livestock and possessions. It drops the key detail of verse 23: they tell their men these things "become ours." They never said that to Jacob's family, and it is how they win the city over. As written, the baker can leave Prep without that detail.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The right answer, "They ask if Shechem should have treated Dinah that way," turns the brothers' closing words, "like a prostitute," into a vague "that way." No other card gives the actual line. The chapter's last line, which card 18 points back to as "a question hanging in the air," never reaches the baker.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
